The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above 2.5% {A1} averaged over 10m {A2}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T04:25:58Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T04:26:20Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 3 minutes 28 seconds {beyond_accounted_for} later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
Broken from 2026-11-11T04:20:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T04:40:12Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 20 minutes 12 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 13 minutes 53 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T04:40:12Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 19.8% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 36.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 18.8% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above 2.5% {A1} averaged over 10m {A2}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9916666666666666% {series_before} before it began, 19.785714285714287% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 36.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 7,773.46 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

Changes to production it read:

  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:

After Argus first acted, logged in 04:27–04:33,04:35–04:37 {Gbac1.8}

  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 18 {G5309.1} occurrences in 18 {G5309.2} minutes, 04:20–04:37 {G5309.3}. After Argus first acted, logged in 04:28,04:31,04:37 {G5309.4}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 8 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 17 {Gce95.3} minutes, 04:21–04:37 {Gce95.4}. After Argus first acted, logged in 04:28,04:31,04:37 {Gce95.5}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of monthly-spend-feature, each in its own words:
      C1: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-11T04:20:05Z {C1.1}. Account page requests then began failing with a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% {C1.2} to about 35% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, refuted]
      C2: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-11T04:20:05Z {C1.5}. This enabled the spend summary path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails about 30% {C1.6} of account page requests. No code or config changed, and no deployment exists. Argus switched the flag off at 2026-11-11T04:25:17Z {C1.7}, but later minutes still show the flag evaluating on and the errors returning. Some evaluations kept serving the on value after the off toggle, so the flag state looks inconsistent. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.9 {C1.8}, refuted, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by the number of purchases where `in_current_month` is true. It does not handle the case where there are none. A shopper who has bought before but not this month brings that number to 0 {F1.1}, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. `render_spend_summary` sends a request to this function when `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false. `serve_account_page` in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches the exception at its boundary and returns a failed page. That is how turning on monthly-spend-feature showed up as account page failures. Turning the flag off hides the bug but leaves it in place.
      
      The change: when no purchases fall in the current month, the function now returns 0 {F1.2}, because the shopper's spend this month really is zero. This is a correct figure, not a swallowed error. The empty case now has a defined answer, and any other failure still reaches the caller. The lifetime average is unchanged, and so is the existing test that expects a shopper with no history at all to raise on the flag-off path. Nothing in account_page.py changes: it still gets an int either way.
      
      The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new cases. One calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` on an account that has past purchases but none this month and asserts 0 {F1.3}. Against the old code that call raises ZeroDivisionError. The other checks the same account through `render_spend_summary` with `use_monthly_summary=True`.
      
      Not covered here: the investigation also reports flag evaluations still returning on after the off toggle. Nothing in this repository evaluates the flag. `render_spend_summary` and `serve_account_page` take the decision as an argument. With this fix, an on evaluation no longer crashes for these shoppers, whatever the flag's state.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #559 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the shopper's month-to-date total by the number of purchases in the current month and has no case for when there are none. A shopper who has bought before but not this month brings that number to {F1.1}, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and `serve_account_page` catches it and returns a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature for the shop's account pages ran a calculation that fails when a shopper has no purchases in the current month, likely shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed.
still_at_risk: Account page requests could keep failing with ZeroDivisionError while monthly-spend-feature evaluates on, and switching the flag off might again leave some minutes evaluating on.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop that every minute's evaluations log monthly-spend-feature=off, with no monthly-spend-feature=on line, and that no account page request fails with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether the switch-off at {P2.1} reached every io-shop flag evaluation. After it, the service still logged minutes in which evaluations returned on ({Gce95.5}), with the ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes ({G5309.4}). If the switch-off did reach every evaluation, find out why the service stayed at the incident's level.
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged a raised account page error rate. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Those requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appears in the logs at the onset and not in the earlier minutes read. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The failing code ran because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. From that minute most flag evaluations returned on. After the flag was switched off at {P2.1}, the error was logged only in the minutes when evaluations still returned on. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: When the flag is on, the code divides by the number of the shopper's purchases in the current month and does not handle the case where there are none. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that served the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The failure in the flag-on code would have been found before any shopper's page used it.
contributing_factors 2: From its first minute, the flag returned on for most evaluations. No smaller staged step was seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Fewer shoppers' pages would have failed, and the rise could have been caught and the flag stopped while only a small share of traffic was exposed.
contributing_factors 3: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told when the alert fired and could have stepped in when switching the flag off did not end the failures.
action_items 1: Require a passing run of io-shop's tests with a feature flag on before that flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 2: Roll out io-shop feature flags in staged steps, starting with a small share of evaluations.
action_items 3: Halt a flag rollout step automatically when the account page error rate rises during it.
action_items 4: Link ErrorRateSustained on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that it pages a person.
went_wrong 1: The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and put monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet the logs after the switch-off showed evaluations still returning on in the same minutes the ZeroDivisionError came, so the flag was left on with the failing code in use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
